report.title: XGBoost is strong on this Tuesday cohort, but not proven best production detector
report.synthesis: XGBoost is not proven the best production detector from this evidence. On the frozen Tuesday development cohort, it had 4 TP, 0 FP, 2 FN, recall 0.667, precision 1.0, AP 0.667, and 2.10 ms P95; several models matched or exceeded recall/AP, and some were faster, though often with many false positives [E1][E3]. Methodology limits matter: the cohort is only 3,413 windows with 6 positives from one correlated campaign, uses a strict unrepaired morning clock, and excluded temporally ineligible observations; this is retrospective offline evidence, not a production holdout [E1][E2]. Score ties are also a caveat: XGBoost had only 2 distinct scores and 99.88% of windows in the largest tie, so threshold ranking is fragile [E2][E3].
next_steps: Validate on an independent holdout or later attack campaigns before any production claim.
Review operating point selection against business cost of false positives versus missed attacks.
Inspect tied-score windows and threshold sensitivity around XGBoost’s two-score output.
Confirm clock eligibility handling for excluded morning observations before comparing models.
